title: Best Golf Courses in Phuket 2026 — 6 Picks | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Six real, currently-open Phuket golf courses for 2026 — Blue Canyon, Red Mountain, Laguna, Loch Palm, Mission Hills and Phuket Country Club. What each course is like, how hard it plays, and tips on booking a tee time.
ogTitle: Best Golf Courses in Phuket 2026 — 6 Picks
ogDesc: Phuket is one of Thailand's most popular golf destinations. Most courses sit in the centre of the island around Kathu or to the north near the airport, all a short drive apart. We have rounded up six courses that are open and actively reviewed in 2026, grouped by style — from demanding championship layouts to easygoing rounds that suit beginners. Every one takes advance bookings, provides caddies, and rents clubs at the clubhouse. Book a morning tee time over the year-end high season: it is cooler and the course is quieter.

blocks.html: Short answer: Strong players who want the toughest test should head to Blue Canyon (its Canyon Course has hosted big tour events) or Red Mountain, with steep elevation changes and big views. For an easier, better-value round, pick Loch Palm or Phuket Country Club. Laguna and Mission Hills make most sense if you are already staying nearby.

items.name: Blue Canyon Country Club
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: Phuket's most famous club, with two 18-hole courses. The Canyon Course hosted the Johnnie Walker Classic three times and is where Tiger Woods won in 1998 — it plays harder and more demanding than the Lakes Course, which has rebuilt greens. It sits in the north of the island, under 15 minutes from the airport. Recent reviews praise the caddies and green conditions, though some note the clubhouse facilities can feel dated.

items.name: Red Mountain Golf Club
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: One of Phuket's most scenic and challenging courses. Opened in 2008 on a former tin mine in Kathu, its signature is dramatic elevation change, red earth against green turf, and old mine scars worked into the design as hazards. It plays to par 72 at around 6,781 yards. Reviews praise the fun, helpful caddies and the unhurried pace, but warn that many holes need real thought before you swing.

items.name: Laguna Golf Phuket
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: An 18-hole, par-71 course inside the Laguna resort complex in the north of the island, near Bang Tao Beach and the Angsana and Banyan Tree hotels. Reviewers rate it among the best-maintained courses in Phuket, with quick greens and fairways cut tighter and firmer than is common in Asia. A marshal keeps pace all day. Green fees run high, but it is very convenient if you are already staying in Laguna.

items.name: Loch Palm Golf Club
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: A par-72 course of about 6,555 yards in the centre of the island in Kathu, right next to Red Mountain and roughly 10 minutes from Phuket Town or Patong. Its calling card is the large Crystal Lake at its heart and lines of palm trees. It plays easier than its sister course Red Mountain, with generous, forgiving fairways. Reviews praise the views, the caddies' help reading lines, and the upkeep — a good pick for a relaxed round.

items.name: Mission Hills Phuket Golf Resort
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: An 18-hole course designed by Jack Nicklaus, opened in 2004 in the Pa Klok area on the island's northeast. Its highlight is a handful of holes that play along the coast with open bay views. There is a driving range and on-site resort accommodation, which makes it a natural stay-and-play choice. Reviews are mixed — some love the stay-then-tee-off mornings, while others find parts of the facility dated.

items.name: Phuket Country Club
items.meta: 🎟️ Book on Klook
items.blurb: The first golf course built in Phuket, open since 1989, in the centre of the island in Kathu and also laid out over a reclaimed tin mine. It offers 27 holes in total plus a driving range. It is a classic resort-style layout without severe elevation, easy to reach, with green fees below the championship courses. Reviews are mixed — some praise the clubhouse and caddies, others flag patchy fairway and green conditions. A fair choice for a round that is not about difficulty.

faq.q: Which Phuket golf course is best for beginners?
faq.a: Go for Loch Palm or Phuket Country Club. Both sit in the centre of the island in Kathu, with gentle elevation and fairly wide, forgiving fairways, and the caddies help you read lines and pick clubs so the round stays relaxed. Blue Canyon's Canyon Course and Red Mountain play much harder and suit accurate players who want a real test.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead, and when is the best time to play?
faq.a: Yes, book in advance — especially morning tee times and over the year-end high season when visitor numbers peak. Booking online ahead usually means a better rate and your choice of start time. November to February is coolest and driest, the best stretch for golf. You can still play in the rainy season, but check the forecast and start early to dodge afternoon showers.

faq.q: How much are green fees in Phuket, and do they include a caddie?
faq.a: Prices vary by course and season. Championship courses like Blue Canyon, Red Mountain and Laguna cost noticeably more than Loch Palm or Phuket Country Club. As is standard in Thailand, a caddie is required and paid separately from the green fee, and a golf cart is usually extra or bundled depending on the course. Check the current rate and what the package includes when you book — low-season deals are common.
